title: For $415k, you can live in a New England community library
author: Megan Johnson
bullets: A former library at 81 Moosup Valley Road, Foster, R.I., is for sale at $415,000.
Built in 1850, the property served as a schoolhouse before becoming Tyler Free Library in 1953.
The 1,760-square-foot building, zoned for agricultural/residential use, features hardwood floors and a fireplace.

title: Patriots 53-man roster projection 1.0: Will New England really stick with 7 receivers?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Patriots' initial 53-man roster includes keeping three quarterbacks: Drake Maye, Tommy DeVito, and Behren Morton.
Running back Terrell Jennings is listed as third choice, while wide receiver Kayshon Boutte remains a potential trade piece.
Veterans Reggie Gilliam and Milton Williams lead fullback and defensive line positions respectively in initial roster projection.

title: Adley Rutschman could make his Red Sox debut in coming days
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Adley Rutschman, 28, was acquired by the Red Sox in a trade with the Orioles on August 3.
Rutschman played two rehab games with Triple-A Worcester after wrist inflammation sidelined him since mid-July.
Rutschman could debut Tuesday in Toronto, while catchers Connor Wong and Jake Rogers are also options.

title: Healey signs bill allowing state to take Norwood Hospital through eminent domain
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Governor Healey signed a bill allowing the state to take Norwood Hospital through eminent domain starting November 1.
The law enables the transfer or lease of the hospital property to a nonprofit for healthcare purposes.
Norwood Hospital has been closed since 2020 floods, with construction stalled due to Steward Health Care's bankruptcy.

title: Dozens displaced by building collapse in Springfield
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A building collapse in Springfield displaced 45 residents after severe thunderstorms and strong winds struck western Massachusetts.
Mayor Domenic J. Sarno declared a state of emergency due to storm damage including power outages and downed trees.
The Red Cross is aiding displaced residents, and extra crews were dispatched to restore power, now back in most areas.

title: Adam Vinatieri jokes about Bill Belichick, Deflategate as part of Hall-of-Fame speech
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Adam Vinatieri was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame, reflecting on his 24-year career and making jokes about key figures.
In his Hall of Fame speech, Vinatieri humorously addressed Bill Belichick and the 'Deflategate' controversy linked to the Patriots.
Vinatieri expressed gratitude towards Patriots fans, recalling their support during the team's successful run and mentioning former teammate Tom Brady.

title: Mass. 7-year-old hit and killed by vehicle while riding bike
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A 7-year-old was killed while riding a bicycle after being hit by a vehicle in Williamstown, Massachusetts on Friday.
The incident occurred at the intersection of Main Street and Buxton Hill Road around 5:40 p.m., according to officials.
No arrests have been made in the case, and the driver was confirmed not impaired by drugs or alcohol, DA's office stated.

title: Residents urged to keep pets out of Stoughton pond after dog’s death
author: Darin Zullo
bullets: Stoughton officials warn residents to keep pets out of Ames Pond after a dog died following a swim there.
The town suspects an algae bloom may have caused the water issues, although E. Coli tests showed no problems.
Cyanobacterial algae blooms can rapidly form and pose health risks to humans and be lethal to pets.

title: Former NH state trooper decertified after misleading police about using GPS to track girlfriend
author: Darin Zullo
bullets: Former NH trooper James Lamoureux decertified and resigns after lying about GPS tracking his girlfriend's car.
Lamoureux pleaded guilty to false reports to law enforcement; his six-month sentence is suspended for two years.
He will be placed on the national registry of decertified officers, barring future law enforcement employment.

title: Man polishing powder horn outside Lexington church prompts bizarre police response
author: Darin Zullo
bullets: Lexington police responded to Grace Chapel for a report of a man with a gun, causing a campus lockdown.
The man, an avid reenactor, was polishing a musket-era powder horn while waiting for his wife outside the church.
Despite initial concerns, police confirmed there was no threat, and the situation was resolved without incident.
